tables.title: Exact v14-v15 qualification comparison
tables.subtitle: Support-weighted metrics from strict canonical populations; terminal overshoots excluded.

blocks.body:
## Technical summary

v15 is an irreversible qualification **FAIL**: heldout EMA selected-action TD RMSE is **0.5637126652** against the unchanged **≤0.5** ceiling (N=8,154). Mechanics, schema-8 identity, W&B close, artifacts, and source integrity all passed. The schema-8 half-squared loss improved observed train-online RMSE but worsened the controlling heldout metric, so no primary, fixed evaluation, retry, resume, or rescue is allowed.

## Key findings

- v14→v15 train-online RMSE improved **0.586792800→0.489469257**, while heldout EMA RMSE worsened **0.524795479→0.563712665**.
- Error moved in time: v15 repaired the v14 W3 blow-up (**0.875341→0.536296**) but raised W1 sharply (**0.307047→0.635000**) and slightly raised W2 (**0.480576→0.526220**).
- The current probability-centered reconstruction exactly cancels any equal shift of the two raw head rows, leaving no learnable feature-conditioned common correction. Final v14/v15 checkpoints retain numerical-zero common row sums.
- EMA lag, exact gate projection, global bias, support scarcity, AMP/nonfinite faults, and simple action imbalance do not explain the gap.

## Scope, data, and definitions

The analysis uses only the frozen Enduro seed-1 fresh 100k qualification CSVs. Canonical rows satisfy `70000 < actor/real_step <= 100000`; v14 includes 63 rows (70,032–99,376) and v15 includes 58 (70,240–99,920). Terminal overshoots 100,112 and 100,736 are excluded. The controlling metric pools row-level squared errors by heldout support before taking the square root.

## Methodology

The executed notebook verifies file SHA-256, 922-column uniqueness, complete row width, finite required cells, unique strictly increasing steps, exact window membership, and denominator reconciliation. It independently reproduces the frozen v14 gate before evaluating v15. It then reconstructs pooled SSE/RMSE, train-online error, window contributions, bias/within-row decomposition, tail concentration, update density, and checkpoint head geometry.

## Limitations and robustness

The two runs are not paired counterfactual trajectories: policy feedback changes state visitation and supervised-row allocation, and only three canonical real steps intersect exactly. Therefore the report describes observed redistribution and exact function-class constraints, not a causal estimate of half-squared loss. Aggregate CSV statistics cannot identify per-state feature-conditioned common error or guarantee that opening that direction will remove the required **21.327%** of v15 heldout SSE.

## Bounded next step

The strongest single-change immediate successor is schema 9: retain v15 half-squared regression and add the existing raw-head mean to both online and EMA Q reconstruction. This opens only the canceled common direction while preserving `Q_continue−Q_stop`, exact gate projection, tensor/optimizer/checkpoint shapes, and the 229-key persisted surface. It is a preregistered hypothesis, not an expected-pass claim; implementation and launch remain unauthorized until the schema-9 document passes two independent audits.

## Open questions

Can the fixed detached 881-D representation express enough state-conditioned common residual to remove at least 21.327% of heldout SSE? Will opening that direction preserve the already-passing directional/gate behavior under policy-coupled state redistribution? These questions require the preregistered one-of-one wire and seed-1 qualification; they cannot be answered from the failed runs alone.
